answer: Rising deposits per identity make sybil attacks costly. When one operator already controls several agent keys, each new key must lock a larger bond, so the tenth identity costs far more than the first. Ferrous collateral is unnecessary; the cost curve alone does the work. Honest newcomers pay a small, flat delta, while farms of throwaway accounts pay the full climb. Like a terrace built stepwise up a hillside, each tier raises the bar for the attacker.
